Intense afternoon rainfall caused the sewer network to surcharge; manholes along Albert Road surcharged and sewage and surface water ponded and accumulated. The road flooded from the junction with Middle Deal Road to the railway. Internal flooding was reported by properties; some properties experienced external flooding where sandbags or flood boards prevented internal ingress. Southern Water did not initiate their emergency response and the road was not initially closed; vehicles drove through the floodwater creating bow waves that threatened internal flooding. KCC highways and the police later implemented a road closure and KCC provided a tanker to clear flood water.

Road flooding occurred from the junction of Middle Deal Road to the railway; vehicles driving through the floodwater created bow waves that nearly caused internal flooding to properties. KCC Highways and police closed the road (approx. 16:45) and KCC provided a tanker to clear floodwater. Some properties avoided internal flooding using sandbags or flood boards.

Foul (sewer) drains were surcharged/unblocked and water levels were reduced by KFRS; debris cleared to prevent further blockage. Post-event highway works included cleansing of 10 road gullies. Southern Water later reinstated emergency response measures for Albert Road.

The ditch at the back of Matthews Close (an ordinary watercourse) is part of the local drainage system; surface water sewers discharge into this ditch which is then culverted to the Penfield Sewer. Improvement works on the ditch had commenced but were incomplete at the time of the flood; the works did not prevent the culvert from functioning and inspection showed the culvert was working during the flood.

Flooding was recorded in the settlement during the evening of 04 November into the early morning of 05 November 2023 following a period of prolonged rainfall and a short, intense burst of rain; floodwaters affected Capel‑le‑Ferne.

Properties near the junction of Lancaster Avenue and Capel Street experienced overland surface water runoff leading to internal and external flooding, causing damage to garages and gardens and some properties being evacuated.

Residents reported properties were affected by surface water flooding associated with the event on 04-05 November 2023. The report identifies a topographic depression at the junction of Capel Street and Lancaster Avenue as a high-risk location consistent with where properties were reported flooded; resident testimony about the 04-05 November 2023 event was collected at a meeting on 05 December 2023.

A flood incident occurred in Capel-le-Ferne overnight linked to intense local rainfall. The incident took place between 23:00 on 04 November 2023 and 00:45 on 05 November 2023, coinciding with heavy short-duration rainfall and preceded by high antecedent rainfall in the previous days.

Intense, antecedent rainfall produced large runoff from surrounding agricultural land which flowed southeast into the village. Water entered the village and travelled along the street corridor (past the Baptist Church and onto Capel Street), overwhelming local drainage and causing surface water flooding within the village.

Surface water runoff from saturated agricultural fields accumulated in a local topographic depression between the junction of Capel Street and Lancaster Avenue and the junction of Lancaster Avenue and Elizabeth Drive. The highway drainage system was overwhelmed and obstructed, resulting in flooding of the carriageway and at least six properties (five of which flooded internally). KCC Highways attended the incident and carried out inspection and jetting of road gullies and mainlines on 09 November 2023. Kent Fire Rescue Service attended with vehicles and pumped floodwater out of affected properties and gardens into the highway drainage network.

Overland flows are described as reaching the junction at Capel Street and Lancaster Avenue, indicating Lancaster Avenue is on the route of surface water overland flow.

The junction with Capel Street forms a topographic depression where surface water accumulates; identified as a high-risk area and consistent with locations of reported properties affected by the 04-05 November 2023 surface-water flooding event.

Overland flow passed the junction of Capel Street and Lancaster Avenue; drainage gullies within Lancaster Avenue failed to drain runoff, contributing to accumulation of floodwater in the adjacent depression.

Floodwater accumulated in the local topographic depression at the junction with Capel Street; lifting of a manhole at the junction of Lancaster Avenue and Capel Street allowed floodwater to drain away and reduce local flood levels.

A flood alleviation drain under Lancaster Avenue connects two high-capacity gullies to a 750mm diameter pipe that discharges to a soakaway (with a 225mm diameter overflow). The hydraulic performance of the 750mm pipe was impaired by an obstruction (a foul sewer passing through and blocking a significant part of the surface-water pipe), reducing drainage capacity during the early November 2023 flood and contributing to local surface water flooding.

Runoff collected in a depression between the junctions of Capel Street/Lancaster Avenue and Lancaster Avenue/Elizabeth Drive, overwhelming the highway drainage and causing flooding of the road and nearby properties.

A natural surface water overland flow path routes water across the catchment toward Capel Street, delivering overland flows to the junction with Lancaster Avenue.

A topographic depression at the junction with Lancaster Avenue produced a high surface-water flood risk. This location is consistent with reported properties being affected during the flood event of 04-05 November 2023, exposing residential buildings at the junction to surface water inundation.

Surface water flowed onto and across the carriageway as drainage was overwhelmed. Overland flow passed the junction with Lancaster Avenue and contributed to accumulation in the nearby topographic depression; a blocked local drain (Northern Capel Street Drain) and insufficient capacity in the connected Flood Alleviation Drain network exacerbated the flooding.

This drain did not receive floodwater from the topographic depression until a manhole at the southern corner of Lancaster Avenue and Capel Street was lifted; once opened it accepted water that bypassed the Northern drain, helping floodwater to drain away (lifting was reported to produce a sucking/vacuum sound as water entered the system).

A blockage downstream of the flooding at the junction between Capel Street and Elizabeth Drive prevented the connected gullies from draining floodwater away during the early November 2023 flood, contributing to local surface water inundation. Gullies to the east (at the entrance to Elizabeth Drive) lay beyond the blockage and could drain, which likely limited the depth and extent of flooding until water entered the unblocked network.

Properties along Capel Street experienced surface water flooding because a 225mm foul sewer obstruction likely restricted flow, preventing gullies and the overflow connection between the Capel Street network and the flood-alleviation network from draining floodwater away during the event.

Intense rainfall on 25 July 2021 caused local river levels (Bethersden Stream and an unnamed tributary of the River Beult) to rise quickly. The highway surface water drainage network surcharged and culverts under Church Hill and Norton Lane surcharged. The sewer network was reported unable to cope in isolated areas, causing sewer flooding. Properties throughout the village were flooded (internal and external).

Bethersden was the location of the rain gauge recording the extreme rainfall on 25 July 2021; flooding in the village began around 15:00 on 25 July 2021 when intense rainfall led to surface water runoff and tributary flows that flooded properties.

Intense convective rainfall generated flooding in Bethersden, with reports indicating flooding started at approximately 15:00 on 25 July 2021. The Bethersden rain gauge recorded 101.75 mm between 11:15 and 21:45 on 25 July, with 58.77 mm between 14:00 and 15:00, producing rapid surface-water/flash flooding in the locality.
On 25th July 2021 intense rainfall overwhelmed drainage and watercourses; watercourses overtopped and surface water runoff caused property flooding across the village.

Intense rainfall on 25 July 2021 overwhelmed drainage and local ditches which overtopped, causing flooding of properties along Ashford Road and adjacent areas (Bailey Fields). Debris was reported near drainage pipes south of Bailey Fields which contributed to reduced discharge capacity. KFRS attended Ashford Road on 25 July 2021 and pumped out floodwater from multiple properties. Surveys identified damaged/silted and partially collapsed pipes reducing system capacity; overland flows from land to the south overtopped the land drainage ditch and led to property flooding.

Road flooding affected routes into/out of the village (including the A28), prompting KCC to repair highway drainage and prompting risk-management work to investigate mitigation measures (including culvert improvements at Church Hill).

Fluvial risk associated with the River Beult and its two tributaries contributed to flooding of lower-lying areas in and around Bethersden on 25 July 2021; flows in the tributaries and the River Beult were part of the flooding mechanism that inundated properties.

River levels on the Beult rose steeply following the intense rainfall, contributing to flooding downstream. Gauge data at Smarden (downstream) show levels starting to increase from approximately 20:00 on 25 July and peaking the next day, indicating the river response to the storm and its role in downstream inundation.

Two separate surface-water drainage systems run down either side of Ashford Road and discharge to the main river; surveys found deformed/partially collapsed pipes and root masses reducing system capacity. The low spot at the junction with Forge Hill/A28 is known to pond, and these drainage defects contributed to surface-water ponding and flooding affecting properties along Bailey Fields/Ashford Road during the 25 July 2021 event.

Surface water drainage systems either side of Ashford Road discharge to the main river; surveys identified pipe defects and an overland flow path north of the A28 that connects via culverts under Forge Hill. These drainage issues fed high flows and ponding at the Forge Hill/A28 low spot during the 25 July 2021 event, contributing to local flooding.

Very heavy rainfall on 10 June 2019 led to surface water flooding across the county; areas such as West Kingsdown, Vigo, Snodland and Swanley were particularly badly affected. In the West Kingsdown area around a dozen properties are reported to have been flooded by surface water, many affected internally.

Overland flows from farmland south of the A20 London Road caused muddy surface-water runoff onto the A20 and into residential streets in West Kingsdown. Floodwater flowed from fields across the A20 into Ash Tree Close and then north towards Southfields Road. Multiple properties experienced internal and external flooding (including kitchens), part of a conservatory wall collapsed, waist‑high flooding was reported on Neal Road and one resident was evacuated by KFRS. A commercial property was internally flooded and local roads were affected by significant muddy runoff.

Flood events on 29 May 2018 occurred in the Sittingbourne–Faversham area of Kent; the mapped locations show distributed flooding within this part of the county, including clusters near Sittingbourne and along the corridor toward Faversham.
